system.notes:
Have you ever wondered why wizards know so many languages? It’s because not every spell is written in Common! Casting spells written in unknown languages can be dangerous, as even a slight deviation from the scroll can lead to unintended consequences. The Mouth of Words knows this from experience! In an attempt at immortality, a real chatterbox of a wizard cast a spell so that “my voice will forever be heard.” Their talkative mouth lives on while still attached to their undead corpse.

AC 12, HP 20, ATK 1 slam +2 (1d6) or 1 spell +3, MV near, S +2, D -2, C +2, I +2, W -2, Ch -3, AL C, LV 4

Undead. Immune to morale checks.

Relentless. If reduced to 0 HP by a non-magical source, DC 15 CON to go to 1 HP instead.

Outer Monologue (INT Spell). DC 12. One target in near can’t stop speaking their inner monologue out loud for 1d4 rounds. Attacks and spellcasting checks are made with DISADV for duration.

Sticks and Stones (INT Spell). DC 13. Creatures within near are berated with insults that really may break bones. They all take 1d6 damage.

Monster design by Michael Putlack. Art by Cameron Maas, 2026.
